input: Buy a film camera and learn to shoot on 35mm

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Budget determines whether the user is looking at entry-level cameras (e.g. Canon AE-1 ~$100) vs. higher-end bodies (e.g. Nikon F3, Leica), and whether they can afford ongoing film and development costs.
Knowing if they want to only shoot film or also develop/scan at home vs. sending to a lab changes the equipment, cost, and skill requirements significantly.
Whether this is self-taught, guided by a friend, or through a class changes the learning path and resources recommended.
The primary shooting subject (portraits, street, landscape, etc.) affects which camera type, lens, and film stock to recommend.
Understanding what 'done well' looks like — a finished roll, a specific number of good shots, or a printed photo — anchors the learning milestones.
Whether they prefer a fully manual camera for learning fundamentals vs. an automatic/semi-automatic camera for ease affects which body to buy.
Knowing whether they plan to buy new, used (online vs. local shop), or borrow affects the immediate first action step in the plan.

gold.taskTitle: Buy a film camera and learn 35mm photography
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to acquire a 35mm film camera and develop the skills to shoot film photography competently.

questions.title: What is your total budget for the camera and first few rolls?
questions.description: Understanding the budget determines which camera bodies are realistic and whether ongoing film and lab costs are factored in.

questions.title: Do you want to develop film yourself or use a lab?
questions.description: This defines the full scope of the task — home development requires additional equipment and chemistry, while a lab keeps it simpler but adds recurring cost.

questions.title: What subjects do you mainly want to photograph?
questions.description: The primary shooting context (street, portraits, landscapes, etc.) shapes the recommended camera type, lens focal length, and film stock.

questions.title: Do you prefer learning fully manual controls or some automation?
questions.description: A preference for full manual (aperture, shutter, focus) vs. aperture-priority or program modes narrows down the right camera body to buy.

questions.title: How do you plan to learn — self-taught, a class, or a mentor?
questions.description: The learning method determines which resources, courses, or communities to include in the plan.

questions.title: What does success look like — a finished roll, a great print, something else?
questions.description: Defining the end goal creates a concrete milestone to work toward and keeps the plan focused.

questions.title: Where do you plan to buy — local camera shop, online, or secondhand?
questions.description: The intended purchase channel determines the immediate first action step and affects what to watch out for (e.g. testing a used body in person).
